utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Lets say we want to add one fourth of this pie to one half of another one

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Cutting pie one fourth and one half are fractions with different denominators

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: To add them we need to find their LCD or lowest common denominator

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Its basically the lowest common multiple of the fractions denominators

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: For our denominators two and four that number is four we want to write all of our fractions as fractions of four

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: One fourth already is and as we saw before one half and two fourths are really the same thing

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Now that we have a common denominator we can just add the numerators two fourths plus one fourth equals three fourths

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Subtraction is the same idea

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: As long as we have a common denominator its just a matter of subtracting the numerators

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: If we dont have a common denominator we find the lowest common denominator and rewrite our fractions to match

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Heres a good example

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Last year Jonahs pies were the highest selling items in the bake sale in fact five ninths of all the students in our school bought them but the year before only five twelfths of the school bought the pies

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Come on it was the first year you made them people didnt know how good they were yet

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Anyway to find out what fraction of students bought the pies the second year but not the first year we would subtract five twelfths from five ninths

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: The denominators are nine and 12 whats the LCD

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Good 36

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Thats the lowest number that both nine and 12 multiply into evenly

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Lets rewrite our fractions as fractions of 36

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Lets see to turn nine into 36 we need to multiply by four which means we also have to multiply the numerator by four and to turn 12 into 36 we multiply by three which means we can also multiply five by three

utterances.Speaker: T
utterances.Sentence: Now we can just subtract the numerators to get our answer between last year and the year before your sales increased by five 36ths
